in his feet x1 week, but it has been getting worse and now is 
radiating up to the knees. Worse with ambulation. No trauma

his feet have also been more swollen recently. Had L PICC

.

increased to 117/56. He received Zosyn 4.5g IV in the ED and one 
ASA 325mg. Guaiac negative stool x1 in ED. EKG showed sinus tach 
with no acute changes.

with probable mild basilar atelectasis. No evidence of fluid

___ LUE U/S of graft: wet read - no thrombosis
 
Brief Hospital Course:
# Fever: In setting of recent line sepsis, it was probable that 
the patient could still be bacteremic. It was found out from 
___ microbiology that the tunneled catheter that was pulled and 
two blood cultures grew out pan-sensitive S. Aureus. The WBC was 
not elevated x2 days, and the lactate was 0.9. The patient's 
hypotension in the ED resolved with 1L NS. The patient's fever 
of 101 trended down without acetaminophen, and by discharge he 
was afebrile x24hrs. The patient received 3 days of vanc and 
Zosyn IV, before signing out AMA. The patient's phone number is 
___ and will be called if cultures are positive.
.
# Anemia: The patient's HCT dropped from 29.1 (baseline in high 
___ to 25.9 on HD#2. On HD#3, the HCT remained stable at 25. 
The patient was guaiac neg x1 in the ED.
.
# ESRD on HD MWF: The patient received HD on ___ without 
problems. However, on the morning of HD#3 (___), the patient's 
AV graft clotted after 30 minutes of HD. The patient was put on 
NPO and sent back to the floor. Renal team called ___ and set up 
the patient for de-clotting. In the meantime, the patient 
rceived a lunch and ate it, so ___ wanted to wait ___ hours 
before doing the procedure. At that time, the patient became 
angry and belligerent, stating that he desired to leave AMA. The 
___ team set up an appointment for thrombosis for ___ ___, which the patient has been to before. He agreed to go 
tomorrow.
.
# Cardiomyopathy (EF ___: The initial troponin was 0.09, in 
setting of chronically elevated troponin, with no EKG changes 
suggesting ischemia or infarct. His home digoxin and ASA were 
continued.
.
# Foot pain: He did not require pain medications for his foot 
pain.
.
# Seizures (last seizure 8 days PTA): He was continued on home 
Keppra and Trileptal doses.
.
# Discharge: The patient signed out AMA after an explanation of 
the reasons for keeping him in the hospital, including pending 
blood cultures and the need for IV antibiotics. He was told that 
the risk of relapse, worse infection or death were possible, and 
he made an informed decision to leave. He explained that if he 
did not go back to work this afternoon that he would be fired 
from his job.
.

breath.  The patient is on hemodialysis.  Evaluate for infiltrate.

Cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable.  Lungs appear essentially clear
bilaterally with probable mild basilar atelectasis.  No evidence of fluid
overload or pleural effusion.  Right-sided rib deformities are again noted.

IMPRESSION:

No significant change aside from removal of left IJ catheter.

STUDY:  Upper extremity arterial duplex.

REASON:  Status post revision of left upper extremity AV graft with fever,
question thrombosis or fluid collection.

FINDINGS:  Duplex evaluation was performed of the left upper extremity AV
graft.  The inflow brachial artery and outflow vein are widely patent.  Graft
velocities range from 234 to 300 cm/sec.  There is no fluid collection seen.

IMPRESSION:  Patent left upper extremity AV graft _____.
